second_order: getting ready for and noticing April Fools
theme_note: Participants anticipate subreddit pranks, recall earlier ones, plan their own, and notice that the room has changed.

second_order: choosing what Smash mark to add next
theme_note: Participants propose, compare, or abandon concrete additions to the shared canvas, from the shine and Fox to lettering and character icons.

second_order: moving canvas coordination into Discord and other channels
theme_note: Participants create, advertise, grow, or redirect helpers into Discord and social channels where plans are coordinated.

second_order: laying out and building pixel plans together
theme_note: Participants supply coordinates, templates, colors, divisions of labor, and direct uptake that turn proposed marks into pixels.

second_order: showing, celebrating, and crediting the mural
theme_note: Participants announce completions, display the shared work, congratulate contributors, and retrospectively credit builders and neighbors.

second_order: repairing, defending, and maintaining the Smash area
theme_note: Participants clean, correct, anti-grief, call defenders, and switch from expansion to keeping existing work intact.

second_order: explaining how to take part in the canvas
theme_note: Participants ask and answer how r/place, pixel timing, locations, and unfamiliar objects such as Goon work.

second_order: working out space, help, and obligations with neighbors
theme_note: Participants negotiate borders, avoid existing art, exchange help, invoke treaties, and name allies or opponents around the Smash area.

second_order: staging and elaborating April Fools claims
theme_note: Participants publish fake results, announcements, guides, leaks, and parody formats, then add lore or supporting turns that keep them going.
Participants test credibility, supply reasons for belief or doubt, recognize tricks, and report being bamboozled.

second_order: returning to tournament, matchup, and game discussion
theme_note: Inside retained threads, participants resume ordinary ranking, results, VOD, matchup, and technical talk after or around the event conduct.

second_order: revealing, restoring, and replaying the pranks
theme_note: Moderators and participants explain what was staged, restore or retain styling, replay the joke, and react after the reveal.

second_order: turning the subreddit into Amazing Crash Family
theme_note: Moderators and participants redraw flairs, rename characters and games, test the altered interface, and inhabit its generic replacement register.

second_order: enforcing and contesting who gets to change the canvas
theme_note: Participants message unscripted editors, forbid work outside Discord plans, contest bans and representation priorities, and argue over lone action versus coordinated authority.

second_order: deciding where r/place posts belong on the subreddit
theme_note: Participants request or reject megathreads, apply posting rules, mark the posting wave as over, and moderate duplicate or ended-event posts.

second_order: recruiting moderators and explaining their work
theme_note: Participants announce applications, ask about timing and responsibilities, describe Discord discussion as moderator work, and commit to apply.
